request: Analyze GSE242294 for PMID 37985354 (MicroRNA-92b in the skeletal muscle regulates exercise capacity via modulation of glucose metabolism.): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.
decision_maker: Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5) Claude Code subagent session

final.primary_estimand: Effect of global miR-92b knockout (M92KO) versus wild-type C57BL/6 on gastrocnemius gene expression in untreated (no exercise) 8-week-old male mice. The paper's RNA-seq is a genotype contrast, not an exercise contrast; exercise enters the paper only through qPCR of miR-92b in trained vs untrained mice (FIG1C-D) and functional running tests, never through this RNA-seq.
planned_contrasts: M92KO vs WT, Gas muscle, n = 3 per group (S3.5.p1, FIG6A-B; paper: 2165 DEGs, 1119 up / 1046 down in M92KO)
final.sample_inclusion: Gas muscle from WT and M92KO mice, n = 3 each (FIG6A); GEO: 8 weeks-old mice without treatment
final.exercise_factor_in_rnaseq: none (GEO characteristics: treatment = '8 weeks-old mice without treatment')
final.normalization: CLC Genomics Workbench read count extraction and normalization (GEO data_processing)
final.paper_method: not_reported (CLC Genomics Workbench per GEO; test not stated)

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: S3.5.p1: 'we performed RNA-seq of Gas muscle samples from WT and M92KO mice ... 2165 DEGs, with a p-value of <0.05 ... 1119 upregulated, 1046 downregulated, in the M92KO mice'. FIG6 legend: n = 3, P < 0.05. S10.p1 deposits GSE242294. S2.1.p1: 8- and 10-week-old male miR-92b-/- mice vs age-matched C57BL/6 WT. The exercise data in the paper (FIG1B-D treadmill training, n = 6) were measured by qPCR only; GSE95735/GSE58248 are reanalyzed external human datasets, not this accession.

checks: S10.p1 names GSE242294 as the paper's deposited sequencing data
genotype WT x3 and miR-92b knockout x3, gastrocnemius, matches FIG6 n = 3 WT vs M92KO Gas
matrix file GSE242294_raw_counts_GAS.txt.gz is the series' only expression file; GSM description names 'raw_counts GAS.txt'

ownership.reasoning: The accession, tissue, genotype groups and n per group all match the paper's RNA-seq description (S3.5.p1, FIG6, S10.p1).

alignment.reasoning: No direct key: matrix columns are C57_8W_GAS_n and b92_8W_GAS_n; GSM descriptions are 'C57-8W-GAS-n,raw_counts GAS.txt' and '92b-8W-GAS-n,raw_counts GAS.txt'. The stem C57 vs 92b/b92 (prefix/suffix 'b' transposed) and replicate number identify each sample uniquely, so both sides are reduced to '<C57|92>_<rep>' by regex (no position-based matching). C57 = WT and 92b = miR-92b knockout agrees with the GSM titles ('WT muscles repN' / 'M92KO muscle repN') and the genotype characteristic. Medium confidence because the KO stem is written 'b92' in the matrix and '92b' in GEO.

matrix.reasoning: integer_fraction 1.0, range 0-1,393,071, median 4; GEO data_processing: 'Supplementary files format and content: tab-delimited text file includes raw counts for each Sample' (CLC Genomics Workbench). The paper does not state the DE input or test.

design.stop_reason: No exercise contrast: GSE242294 contains only untreated (no exercise) WT vs miR-92b knockout gastrocnemius (GEO treatment '8 weeks-old mice without treatment'; paper S3.5.p1/FIG6). Every sample is sedentary, so the effect of exercise on gene expression is not identifiable from these data. The only analyzable contrast (KO vs WT) is a genotype effect and is not the requested estimand; the paper's exercise evidence (FIG1 trained vs untrained) is qPCR of miR-92b only and was not sequenced.

final.available_contrast: genotype KO vs WT, all sedentary (not an exercise estimand)

candidates.value: genotype_raw KO vs WT as an exercise proxy
candidates.reason_rejected: A knockout that changes exercise capacity is not an exercise exposure; reporting it as 'how exercise affects gene expression' would misstate the estimand.

design.reasoning: Request asks for the effect of exercise. Metadata has one grouping column (genotype) and a constant treatment field 'without treatment'; paper S3.5.p1 and FIG6 describe the RNA-seq as WT vs M92KO only; exercise appears only in qPCR (FIG1B-D) and functional tests. Refused at design per the skill's stop rule (sequenced sample set with no exercise arm).

discrepancies.paper: paper title and question concern exercise capacity; exercise training only in qPCR experiments (FIG1)
discrepancies.data: all six GEO samples untreated (no exercise)
